concepts.title: Nerve or root?
concepts.body: A **peripheral nerve** carries fibres from several roots to a defined set of muscles and skin. A nerve lesion weakens **its** muscles and numbs **its** sensory area — which rarely matches a single dermatome or myotome.
concepts.ur: Nerve ka area aur root ka area alag hai — isi se pehchaan hoti hai ke masla nerve mein hai ya root mein.

concepts.title: The hand's three nerves in 30 seconds
concepts.body: **Radial** — extend the wrist and fingers (“stop” sign); sensation on the back of the first web space. **Median** — thumb up from the palm and the “OK” sign; sensation at the index fingertip. **Ulnar** — spread the fingers and grip paper (Froment); sensation at the little fingertip.

concepts.title: Test the autonomous zones
concepts.body: Each nerve has an **autonomous zone** that only it supplies — test there for a clear answer: index fingertip (median), little fingertip (ulnar), first dorsal web space (radial), lateral upper arm (axillary), first web space of the foot (deep fibular), sole (tibial).

concepts.title: Brachial plexus patterns
concepts.body: Plexus lesions mix nerves and roots.

head: Lesion
Pattern
rows: Arm hangs adducted and internally rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated ('waiter's tip')
Weak intrinsic hand muscles, claw hand ± Horner's syndrome

concepts.title: Classic lesion signs
bullets: **Wrist drop** — radial nerve at the spiral groove.
**Claw hand** — ulnar nerve (ring and little fingers).
**Thenar wasting / ape hand** — median nerve at the wrist.
**Medial winging** — long thoracic; **lateral winging** — spinal accessory.
**Foot drop with normal inversion** — common fibular at the fibular neck.
**Trendelenburg** — superior gluteal nerve or weak gluteus medius.
concepts.body: Learn these patterns by sight — examiners love them.

concepts.title: The ulnar paradox
concepts.body: A **low** ulnar lesion (wrist) gives **more** clawing than a **high** one (elbow). In a high lesion the ulnar half of FDP is also paralysed, so the fingertips can't curl — the claw looks milder even though more is lost.

concepts.title: Neurodynamic tests
concepts.body: Neurodynamic tests load the nervous system with a sequence of movements. A test is **positive** when it reproduces the patient's symptoms, differs from the other side and the symptoms change with **structural differentiation** (moving a distant joint that affects the nerve but not the local tissue).

head: Test
Nerve bias
Sequence (simplified)
rows: Shoulder depression, abduction 110°, wrist/finger extension, supination, ER, elbow extension
Shoulder girdle depression, elbow extension, ER, supination, wrist/finger extension, shoulder abduction
Depression, elbow extension, internal rotation, pronation, wrist/finger flexion, ulnar deviation
Wrist/finger extension, pronation, elbow flexion, ER, abduction, depression
Passive hip flexion with knee straight; add ankle dorsiflexion; positive 30–70°
Sitting slump, neck flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion; release neck flexion
Prone, passive knee flexion; anterior thigh symptoms

concepts.title: Separating nerve, root and plexus
concepts.body: Find a muscle that shares the **root** but not the **nerve**. Weak APB (median) + normal FPL (also median, higher branch) = carpal tunnel. Weak APB + weak FPL + weak pronator teres = high median lesion. Weak APB + weak triceps + numb middle finger = C7–C8 root or lower plexus. Nerve conduction studies confirm.

cards.front: Wrist drop is caused by a lesion of the…
cards.back: Radial nerve. The radial nerve supplies the wrist and finger extensors.

cards.front: Which nerve supplies the deltoid?
cards.back: Axillary. Axillary nerve: deltoid and teres minor.

cards.front: The median nerve's best sensory test site is…
cards.back: The index fingertip (palmar). The palmar index tip is supplied only by the median nerve.

cards.front: Foot drop after a tight below-knee cast suggests the…
cards.back: Common fibular nerve. The common fibular nerve wraps around the fibular neck.

cards.front: Froment's sign tests…
cards.back: Adductor pollicis (ulnar nerve). The thumb IP flexes (FPL, median) to compensate for weak adductor pollicis.

cards.front: Erb's palsy affects which part of the plexus?
cards.back: Upper trunk (C5–C6). Upper trunk: 'waiter's tip' posture.

cards.front: Medial winging of the scapula = weakness of…
cards.back: Serratus anterior (long thoracic nerve). Serratus anterior holds the medial border against the chest wall.

cards.front: Burning anterolateral thigh with normal strength suggests…
cards.back: Meralgia paraesthetica (lateral femoral cutaneous). A purely sensory nerve compressed near the ASIS.

cards.front: Why can a low ulnar lesion look more clawed than a high one?
cards.back: In high lesions ulnar FDP is also weak, so the fingertips can't curl. The ulnar paradox.

cards.front: Mid-shaft humerus fracture with wrist drop: where is the radial nerve injured?
cards.back: Spiral groove. The radial nerve lies in the spiral groove of the humerus.

cards.front: Foot drop with normal hip abduction and normal inversion suggests…
cards.back: Common fibular nerve lesion. Superior gluteal (hip abduction) and tibial (inversion) are spared.

cards.front: A positive Trendelenburg sign points to weakness of…
cards.back: Gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve). The pelvis drops on the unsupported side.

cards.front: Which neurodynamic test biases the median nerve?
cards.back: ULNT1. ULNT1 (and 2a) bias the median nerve.

cards.front: A neurodynamic test is positive when…
cards.back: It reproduces symptoms, differs from the other side and changes with structural differentiation. Stretch discomfort alone is not a positive test.

cards.front: Numb index fingertip and weak APB, but FPL and pronator teres are strong. — Lesion site?
cards.back: Median nerve at the wrist (carpal tunnel). Branches above the wrist are spared.

cards.front: SLR reproduces buttock and calf pain at 40°; adding ankle dorsiflexion worsens it; releasing hip flexion slightly eases it. — Interpretation?
cards.back: Positive neurodynamic test — sciatic nerve/L5–S1 root sensitivity. Symptom reproduction with structural differentiation (ankle DF) supports neural involvement.

cards.front: Weak shoulder abduction, elbow flexion and external rotation; numb lateral arm and forearm after a motorbike fall onto the shoulder. — Most likely lesion?
cards.back: Upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6, Erb's). Several C5–C6 nerves (axillary, suprascapular, musculocutaneous) together = upper trunk.

cards.front: Wrist drop, but triceps strength and the triceps reflex are normal; numb dorsal first web space. — Where is the radial nerve injured?
cards.back: Spiral groove of the humerus — below the triceps branches. Triceps spared + sensory loss = spiral groove; PIN lesions have no sensory loss.

cards.front: Claw hand of the ring and little fingers with weak finger abduction, but normal sensation and strong FDP to the little finger. — Lesion site?
cards.back: Deep (motor) branch of the ulnar nerve at Guyon's canal. Sensory sparing and strong ulnar FDP place it distally — the deep motor branch at the wrist.

cards.front: Tingling in the thumb and index finger at night; positive Phalen's and Tinel's at the wrist; normal neck movements and reflexes. — Best next step?
cards.back: Treat as carpal tunnel syndrome (night splint, education) and refer for nerve conduction if severe or persistent. Classic median nerve compression at the wrist; conservative care first unless wasting or severe.
